Trial 200 was a single arm, Phase 1/2, open label trial that enrolled patients with CML in one of its three stages: CP, AP, and BP or Ph+ ALL.

design.text: Single-arm, open-label, multicenter 2-part trial (dose escalation Part 1, efficacy Part 2)

citations.quote: A single-arm, Phase 1/2 open-label, multicenter trial was conducted to evaluate the efficacy and safety of BOSULIF 500 mg once daily in patients with imatinib-resistant or -intolerant CML with separate cohorts for chronic, accelerated, and blast phase disease previously treated with one prior TKI (imatinib) or more than one TKI (imatinib followed by dasatinib and/or nilotinib).
The trial consisted of two parts, a dose escalation part (Part 1) and an efficacy part (Part 2).

population.text: Adult patients with Ph+ chronic, accelerated, or blast phase CML (and Ph+ ALL) with resistance or intolerance to prior therapy (imatinib +/- dasatinib/nilotinib)

citations.quote: The single-arm Phase 1/2 clinical trial enrolled patients with Ph+ chronic, accelerated, or blast phase chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) and Ph+ acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) with resistance or intolerance to prior therapy.

endpoint.text: For CP CML: rate of major cytogenetic response (MCyR) at week 24 and duration of MCyR; for AP/BP CML: confirmed complete hematologic response (CHR) and overall hematologic response (OHR)

citations.quote: The efficacy endpoints for patients with CP CML previously treated with one prior TKI (imatinib) were the rate of attaining MCyR at week 24 and the duration of MCyR.
patients with previously treated AP and BP CML were confirmed complete hematologic response (CHR) and overall hematologic response (OHR).

n.text: 546 treated CML patients (503 evaluable for efficacy)

citations.quote: The trial enrolled 546 patients with CP, AP or BP CML. Of the total patient population 73% were imatinib resistant and 27% were imatinib intolerant.
Of the 546 treated patients, 503 were considered evaluable for efficacy.

result.text: CP CML prior imatinib only (N=266): MCyR at 24 weeks 33.8% (95% CI 28.2, 39.9); CP CML prior imatinib + dasatinib/nilotinib (N=108): MCyR by 24 weeks 26.9% (95% CI 18.8, 36.2); AP CML (N=69): OHR 55.1% (95% CI 42.6, 67.1); BP CML (N=60): OHR 28.3% (95% CI 17.5, 41.4)

indication.text: Treatment of adult patients with chronic, accelerated, or blast phase Ph+ chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) with resistance or intolerance to prior therapy

citations.quote: BOSULIF is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with chronic, accelerated, or blast phase Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph+) chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) with resistance or intolerance to prior therapy.

target_moa.text: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor that inhibits the abnormal Bcr-Abl kinase driving CML as well as Src-family kinases (Src, Lyn, Hck), with minimal inhibition of PDGF receptor and c-Kit

citations.quote: Bosutinib belongs to a pharmacologic class of drugs called TKIs. It inhibits the abnormal Bcr-Abl kinase that promotes CML as well as the Src-family of kinases including Src, Lyn and Hck. Bosutinib causes minimal inhibition of PDGF receptor and c-Kit.

Wyeth submitted this application for bosutinib, an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor, for the treatment of chronic, accelerated, or blast phase Ph + chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in adult patients with resistance or intolerance to prior therapy.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) included diarrhea (82%), nausea (46%), thrombocytopenia (41%), vomiting (39%), abdominal pain (37%), rash (35%), anemia (27%), pyrexia (26%) and fatigue (24%); serious reactions include myelosuppression, GI toxicity (diarrhea), fluid retention, hepatotoxicity and rash

citations.quote: Serious adverse reactions reported include anaphylactic shock [see *Contraindications (4)]*, myelosuppression, gastrointestinal toxicity (diarrhea), fluid retention, hepatotoxicity and rash.

vote.text: No advisory committee was convened; the product was not taken to an Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee Meeting

citations.quote: This product was not taken to an Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee Meeting.

detail.text: Approved first cycle; the reviewer recommended regular approval and no prior CRL for this application is noted

citations.quote: This reviewer recommends regular approval of Bosulif (bosutinib) for the treatment of chronic, accelerated, or blast phase Philadelphia chromosome positive (Ph+) chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in adult patients with resistance to, or intolerance of prior therapy.

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated November 17, 2011, received November 17, 2011, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for BOSULIF® (bosutinib) Tablets, 100 mg and 500 mg.

requirement.text: PMR 1912-1: Conduct a drug-drug interaction trial to evaluate the effect of a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor (e.g. erythromycin) on the pharmacokinetics of bosutinib

citations.quote: PMR 1912-1 Conduct a drug-drug interaction trial to evaluate the effect of a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor (e.g. erythromycin) on the pharmacokinetics of bosutinib. The proposed protocol must be submitted for review and concurrence prior to trial initiation.

requirement.text: PMC 1912-2: Continue follow-up of patients enrolled in Study 200-WW at least an additional 2 years past the March 28, 2011 cut-off date, submitting a Final Report with data through March 28, 2013

citations.quote: 1912-2 Continue follow-up of patients (on treatment and in protocol defined post-treatment follow-up) enrolled in Study 200-WW at least an additional 2 years past the March 28, 2011 cut-off date. Submit the Final Report, which will consist of an updated report containing, at a minimum, data through March 28, 2013.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation for this CML indication (making the application exempt from PREA pediatric assessment)

citations.quote: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: Bosutinib received regular (full) approval based on single-arm Trial 200 using major cytogenetic response as the efficacy endpoint; the product has orphan drug designation and was not taken to an advisory committee; the prior Phase 3 Trial 3000 in newly diagnosed CP-CML failed its primary endpoint.

citations.quote: This reviewer recommends regular approval of Bosulif (bosutinib) for the treatment of chronic, accelerated, or blast phase Philadelphia chromosome positive (Ph+) chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in adult patients with resistance to, or intolerance of prior therapy.
Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.
Trial 3000 was a failed trial that did not demonstrate the superiority of bosutinib over imatinib in the newly diagnosed setting.

description.text: Added a new dosing regimen to the Dosage and Administration section

citations.quote: The Prior Approval Supplement 007 provides for updates to the US Prescribing Information (USPI) Dosage and Administration section to include new dosing regimen. In addition, updates to the USPI Clinical Studies section related to the final study report and fulfillment of postmarketing commitment 1912-2: Continue follow-up of patients (on treatment and in protocol defined posttreatment follow-up) enrolled in Study 200-WW.

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of adult patients with newly-diagnosed chronic phase Ph+ CML (accelerated approval)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication for the treatment of adult patients with newly-diagnosed chronic phase (CP) Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myelogenous leukemia (Ph+ CML).

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to regular approval for newly diagnosed Ph+ chronic phase CML in adults

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for regular approval of the treatment of adult patients with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome positive (Ph+) Chronic phase (CP), chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) indication. In addition, this supplement provides updates to the United States Prescribing Information (USPI) in the Adverse Reactions, Warnings and Precautions, Nonclinical Toxicology, Clinical Studies, and Patient Labeling sections based upon results from the BFORE trial (Study 1053).

description.text: Added new pediatric indication for patients 1 year and older with chronic phase Ph+ CML (newly-diagnosed or resistant/intolerant to prior therapy)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a request for pediatric exclusivity, along with a new pediatric indication for the treatment of pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with chronic phase (CP) Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myelogenous leukemia (Ph+ CML), newly-diagnosed or resistant or intolerant to prior therapy.
